heading: INT. ABANDONED ANTARCTIC WEATHER STATION - DAY

units.text: INT. ABANDONED ANTARCTIC WEATHER STATION - DAY
A single room the size of a train carriage.
Frost on the inside of the windows.
A pegboard of rusted instruments, a cot with a sleeping bag, a radio set under a tarp.
The wind outside is a long low voice, never stopping.
HESTER VANTONGEREN, fifties, hair cropped short and gone white, face seamed by weather and something older.
A green parka, hood down, fingerless gloves.
She has been here four days.
She sits at the radio with a pencil.
She has a notebook.
She writes a column of numbers, stops, crosses it out, writes another.
On the shelf beside the set: a battered cassette recorder, one red light glowing.
She presses PLAY.
Day one. Landed on schedule. Station intact. Heater functional. Supplies for three weeks, if I'm careful.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Hester pauses it.
She looks at the cot.
At the neat blankets, the folded socks beneath them.
She presses PLAY again.
Day two. Wind picking up. Radio silent but the batteries are fresh. I will try again at noon.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: She switches it off.
She gets up.
At the window she scrapes frost with a thumbnail until a little clear patch opens, white on white, a sky and a ground with no seam between them.
She opens the stove.
One log left.
She holds it for a moment, weighing it, then puts it back and closes the door.
She returns to the radio.
Turns a dial.
Static.
She keys the mic.
Station Ember, Station Ember. Anyone.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Static.
She releases the key.
She does not repeat.
She sits for a long minute with her hands flat on the table.
Then she picks up the pencil and writes, very slowly, in the notebook: DAY FIVE.
She stops.
She presses the recorder's RECORD button.
The red light shifts.
Day five. Wind steady. I'm fine.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: She lets the tape run for several seconds of silence.
The wind fills it.
Then she turns the recorder off, picks up the last log, and carries it to the stove.
